reading.review:
Infectiously curious and genuinely laugh-out-loud funny. Transcribed from conversations with Ralph Leighton, these anecdotes follow Nobel laureate Richard Feynman through radio repair, safecracking, bongo drumming, Mayan hieroglyphs, and the joy of figuring things out from first principles.

A wonderful antidote to taking oneself too seriously.

note.note-text: The wobbling cafeteria plate that reignited his joy in physics and led directly to his Nobel-winning work on quantum electrodynamics.
Cargo Cult Science — 'The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.'
